title: Clamp two boards edge to edge by pumping a one-hand bar clamp's trigger
instruction: Clamp the two pine boards together edge to edge with the red bar clamp, then let go of the clamp.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00, about 890,000 US workers) "assemble and fasten materials ... using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue" (O*NET task statement). Every glued joint is held in clamps until the glue sets, so clamping is part of nearly every glued assembly they build: edge-joining boards into a wider panel for a shelf, a stair tread, a countertop or a cabinet side. The one-hand bar clamp is their standard clamp for it because it is set and tightened with one hand: the jaws are placed round the work and the trigger is squeezed stroke by stroke, each stroke driving the bar a few millimetres, until the joint is closed and pressed, and the clamp then holds the force on its own.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Work mat: dark grey rubber, 46 x 40 cm (46 along x), 3 mm, fixed, at (0.34, -0.02). Boards: two pine boards, 20 x 6 x 1.8 cm (20 along x), 108 g each, lying flat side by side on the mat, long edges 2 mm apart, ends aligned: right board at (0.429, -0.090), left board at (0.429, -0.028). Bar clamp: a red 6 in one-hand bar clamp (0.32 kg; 62 mm throat), lying flat on the mat in front of the boards, its steel bar (16 x 4.8 mm, 231 mm) along y, jaws opened 14 cm and pointing forward (+x), their tips 2.2 cm in front of the boards' near ends; the fixed jaw's pad face at y -0.125 (5 mm off the right board), the moving jaw's at y 0.015 (13 mm off the left board); the black pistol grip (88 x 25 x 22 mm, centre (0.174, -0.175)) and the red trigger (74 x 12 x 16 mm, in front of the grip on the +y side) point at the robot. Mechanism: the trigger pivots in the handle (0 to 23 degrees, a torsion spring holds it open with 8 N at 4 cm); its drive arm, 9 mm from the pivot, pushes the bar through the handle (3.5 mm per full squeeze, a drive plate that slips back when the trigger springs open), and a brake lets the bar slide shut but never back open. The fixed jaw's black rubber pad (40 x 20 x 5 mm) is a spring of 40 N per mm with 3 mm of travel. A rubber mallet (39 cm) at (0.585, 0.33) along y and a steel speed square (29 x 22 cm) at (0.58, -0.40), fixed. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Clamping force: the fixed jaw's pad compression times 40 N per mm (a pad that only rests on a board reads 0 N). Jaw gap: the least distance from three points on each pad (centre and 18 mm either side) to the outer edge of the board it presses. Joint gap: the joint's widest opening at the boards' ends. Round the panel: both pad centres 1 cm or more inside the boards' ends and within their thickness. Closed: round the panel, both jaw gaps and the joint gap 0.5 mm or less. Clamped: closed with 20 N or more. 1.0: clamped, the boards' ends within 3 mm and their tops level within 1 mm, no finger within 3 cm of the clamp or the boards, the clamp and boards still (under 0.5 mm and 0.01 rad over 0.5 s), all held without a break for 1 s. 0.75: clamped, not yet all of that. 0.5: closed, under 20 N. 0.25: round the panel only. 0 otherwise or if a part falls off the table. Real trial: a thin load cell or force film (0 to 200 N, 3 mm or less) between the fixed jaw's pad and the right board must read 20 N or more for 1 s after the grippers are clear; feeler gauge 0.5 mm, straightedge 1 mm, tape measure, video for the rest.
reset_notes: Press the clamp's release lever, open its jaws to 14 cm, lay it flat at its start, and lay the boards back side by side with their edges 2 mm apart and their ends aligned.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics (32/8 solver iterations for the clamp and boards), 20 Hz control. Boards are boxes dressed in pine meshes; the clamp is boxes on joints: a hinged trigger with a torsion spring, a bar on a slide, a one-way joint for the drive plate. The drive and brake plates are stops moved every control step (0.1 mm teeth), not tilting plates gripping by friction. One 40 N/mm spring on the fixed pad stands for the flex of jaws, bar and pads. Dry joint, no glue.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,200 steps: no finger came within 3 cm of the clamp or the boards). Demo: 1.0 (success at step 250, the trigger squeezed in strokes, 87 N held after the release). Pushing the jaw shut by hand instead of the trigger: 0.5 (1.3 N at most).
